title: Evidence Standard for an Allowed Claim — Travel Protection Plans
content:
The allowance on the insurer's last decision is taken, when a settlement is rated on a Travel Protection Plans certificate, at a share which the evidence supporting the claim carries. Two things decide that share: whether the claim the insurer allowed names the evidence that supports it, and whether that evidence reached the insurer within the plan's deadline for supporting documents counted from the day the claim was filed. The days counted are the whole calendar days from the day the claim was filed to the day the insurer reached its decision.

Where the claim the insurer allowed names the evidence that supports it and that evidence reached the insurer within the plan's deadline for supporting documents counted from the day the claim was filed, the share which the evidence supporting the claim carries is the whole of the allowance, 100 per cent.

Where the claim the insurer allowed names the evidence that supports it and that evidence reached the insurer after that deadline, the share which the evidence supporting the claim carries is 75 per cent.

Where neither holds, the share which the evidence supporting the claim carries is 50 per cent.

## The plan's deadline for supporting documents

| Plan | Deadline for supporting documents, calendar days from the filing |
| --- | --- |
| Trip Basics Essential | 30 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 30 |
| TripGuard Plus | 60 |
| TripGuard Premier | 90 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 90 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 60 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 90 |

## Both sides of the deadline

On a plan whose deadline for supporting documents is 60 calendar days, a claim filed and decided 60 days later, naming the evidence that supports it, falls within the deadline, because the comparison is within-the-deadline and the boundary day itself satisfies it: the share is 100 per cent. The same claim decided 61 days after filing falls after the deadline, and the share is 75 per cent.

Where the claim the insurer allowed names no evidence at all, neither of the first two cases is reached whatever the dates show, and the share is 50 per cent.
